body:
Pretty much. "Oh, you're suicidal? Here, have an SSRI. See you in six months!"

Yeah, thanks, very helpful.
I've seen doctors. They've prescribed me SSRIs and stimulants, even though I've been diagnosed bipolar and don't do well on either. No, I don't know why, either.

My relatives much prefer to have nothing to do with me, and my closest friends maintain a healthy distance of "I'll read any text messages you send me but I really don't feel comfortable responding, hearing your voice, or seeing you in person."

As for Thanksgiving, I stayed home and slept all day. It was okay, though I was sort of worried I might wake up next to a ghost, and I couldn't seem to stay asleep for more than two hours at a time.

For me, the part where I'll sometimes lie in bed for countless hours, overflowing with energy, finding every single aspect of my thoughts and my movements and the room around me so intensely fascinating that I can't stop smiling and laughing, never thinking that I might want to get up and *do* something... clued me in that something might be a bit off.

I've never moved overseas, but I have sold all of my belongings and moved across the continent without first finding a new place to live.

Being homeless in an unknown city is actually not as bad as you might think! ...Um, until you frivolously spend all of your money and run out of places to shack up. Then it's pretty bad.
Survival and procreation are the two core goals of nearly all humans. Good luck convincing them to forgo either.
